relations.definition: To share a common boundary or border with another entity.
relations.embedding_query_text: has border with: To share a common boundary or border with another entity.

candidates.label: geoTouches
candidates.comment: A geo touches relation representing a symmetric spatial relationship where two geometries or places share at least one boundary point but no interior points. Also called: borders, adjoins, meets at boundary. Examples: "Country A" geo touches "Country B", "Property Line 1" geo touches "Property Line 2", "Lake Shore" geo touches "Land Mass". Distinct from geoIntersects, which can share interior points.

candidates.label: geoEquals
candidates.comment: A geo equals relation representing a symmetric spatial relationship where two geometries or places are topologically identical, sharing the same interior and boundary without intersecting each other's exterior. Also called: identical to, same location as, equivalent geometry. Examples: "City Boundary A" geo equals "City Boundary B (updated)", "Park Outline (old)" geo equals "Park Outline (new)", "Country Shape (vector)" geo equals "Country Shape (raster)".

candidates.label: geoIntersects
candidates.comment: A geo intersects relation representing a spatial relationship where two geometries or places share at least one common point. Also called: overlaps with, touches, crosses. Examples: "River 'Thames'" geo intersects "City 'London'", "Road 'Main Street'" geo intersects "Park 'Central Park'", "Country 'USA'" geo intersects "Country 'Canada'". Distinct from geoDisjoint, which has no points in common.

candidates.label: geoOverlaps
candidates.comment: A geo overlaps relation representing a spatial relationship where two geometries or places share some, but not all, common points. Also called: partially overlaps, shares area with, intersects partially. Examples: "City Park" geo overlaps "Residential Area", "Forest Reserve" geo overlaps "Hiking Trail Network", "Economic Zone A" geo overlaps "Economic Zone B". Distinct from geoContains (one fully encloses the other) and geoDisjoint (no common points).

candidates.label: geoDisjoint
candidates.comment: A geo disjoint relation representing a symmetric spatial relationship where two geometries or places have no points in common and are entirely disconnected. Also called: separate from, not overlapping, unconnected. Examples: "Country 'USA'" geo disjoint "Country 'China'", "Island 'Hawaii'" geo disjoint "Continent 'Europe'", "Building 'A'" geo disjoint "Building 'B'". Distinct from geoIntersects, which has at least one point in common.

candidates.label: geoContains
candidates.comment: A geo contains relation representing a spatial relationship where one geometry or place fully encloses another, with at least one interior point in common. Also called: encloses, encompasses, includes. Examples: "Country 'France'" geo contains "City 'Paris'", "Continent 'Europe'" geo contains "Country 'Germany'", "Building 'Empire State'" geo contains "Office 'Suite 100'". Distinct from geoWithin, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: hasRepresentation
candidates.comment: A representation relation between a biochemical entity and its common symbolic or structural representation. Also called represented by, symbolic form, structural representation. Examples: "A BioChemEntity has a representation as a chemical structure.", "The entity has a representation as a text sequence.", "This biochemical entity has a URL representation."

candidates.label: geoCovers
candidates.comment: A geo covers relation representing a spatial relationship where one geometry or place completely covers another, meaning every point of the covered entity is within the covering entity. Also called: covers, encompasses, overlies. Examples: "Country 'France'" geo covers "City 'Paris'", "North America" geo covers "Lake 'Superior'", "City 'Springfield'" geo covers "House '123 Main St'". Distinct from geoCoveredBy, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: geoCrosses
candidates.comment: A geo crosses relation representing a spatial relationship where two geometries or places intersect, sharing some but not all interior points, and their intersection has a lower dimension than at least one of them. Also called: intersects, traverses, cuts across. Examples: "River 'Mississippi'" geo crosses "State 'Missouri'", "Road 'Route 66'" geo crosses "City 'Chicago'", "Flight Path" geo crosses "Mountain Range".

candidates.label: connectedTo
candidates.comment: A connection relation between an anatomical structure and other anatomical structures it is connected to. Also called "linked to", "adjoins", "connects with". Examples: "Femur anatomical structure connectedTo Tibia", "Brain anatomical structure connectedTo Spinal cord".

relations.definition: To go to a place for a short time, often for a specific purpose or to see someone.
relations.embedding_query_text: visited: To go to a place for a short time, often for a specific purpose or to see someone.

chosen_property.label: visited
chosen_property.definition: To go to a place for a short time, often for a specific purpose or to see someone.
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property fits the relation of visiting a place

candidates.label: touristType
candidates.comment: A tourist type relation between a tourist attraction, destination, or trip and the specific audience or type of tourist it is suitable for. Also called target tourist, suitable for, visitor type. Examples: "TouristAttraction touristType 'children'", "TouristDestination touristType 'adventure seekers'", "TouristTrip touristType 'visitors from Japan'".

candidates.label: displayLocation
candidates.comment: A display location relation between a creative work or product and the place where it can be viewed or experienced in-person. Also called "viewing location", "exhibition place", "experience venue". Examples: "Painting 'Mona Lisa' displayLocation 'Louvre Museum'", "Product 'New Car Model' displayLocation 'Dealership Showroom'", "Sculpture displayLocation 'Art Gallery'".

candidates.label: attendee
candidates.comment: A person or organization present at an event. Also called: participant, guest, visitor. Examples: "Event 'Concert' attendee 'John Doe'", "Event 'Conference' attendee 'Acme Corp'", "Event 'Meeting' attendee 'Jane Smith'". Distinct from attendees, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: publicAccess
candidates.comment: A public access relation indicating whether a place is open to public visitors. Also called open to public, publicly accessible. Examples: "A park has public access 'true'.", "A private residence has public access 'false'.", "A museum has public access 'true'."

candidates.label: attendees
candidates.comment: A person present at an event. Also called: participants, guests, visitors. Examples: "Event 'Concert' attendees 'John Doe'", "Event 'Conference' attendees 'Acme Corp'", "Event 'Meeting' attendees 'Jane Smith'". Distinct from attendee, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: toLocation
candidates.comment: A destination location relation between an action (like exercise, insert, move, or transfer) and the final place of the object or agent after the action. Also called destination, final location, arrival place. Examples: "MoveAction toLocation 'New York'", "TransferAction toLocation 'Warehouse B'", "ExerciseAction toLocation 'gym'". Distinct from location, which is the general place where something is or occurs.

candidates.label: itinerary
candidates.comment: A travel plan relation between a trip and the sequence of places or an item list detailing the destinations. Also called travel route, trip plan, destinations, journey path. Examples: A trip has an itinerary of 'Paris, Rome, London'. A trip has an itinerary of an ItemList detailing stops. A vacation package has an itinerary of 'Hawaii'.

candidates.label: homeLocation
candidates.comment: A home location relation between a person and their residential contact point or place. Also called residence, dwelling, home address. Examples: "A person has a home location in London.", "Her home location is a specific address.", "The individual's home location is a contact point."

candidates.label: subTrip
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a larger trip and a smaller trip that is a component or segment of it. Also called "trip segment", "part of trip", "daily itinerary", "trip leg". Examples: "The multi-day journey has subTrip Day 1", "The grand tour's subTrip is the visit to Rome", "This trip includes several subTrip components."

candidates.label: partOfTrip
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a trip and a larger, multi-day trip it is a segment of. Also called is a segment of, is a day of, is a leg of, belongs to. Examples: Day 1 of a vacation is part of the overall trip. A specific excursion is part of a larger travel itinerary. A flight segment is part of a multi-leg journey.

relations.definition: To hold the office or position of president in an organization or entity.
relations.embedding_query_text: is president of: To hold the office or position of president in an organization or entity.

chosen_property.label: isPresidentOf
chosen_property.definition: To hold the office of president in an organization or country.
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property fits the relation of being a president of a city

candidates.label: hasCertification
candidates.comment: A certification relation between an entity (organization, person, place, product, or service) and its associated certification. Also called holds certification, certified by, possesses certification, has accreditation. Examples: "An organization has a certification for quality management.", "A product has a certification for organic ingredients.", "A person has a certification in project management."

candidates.label: namedPosition
candidates.comment: A specific named position or role played by a person or organization within a larger organization. Also called role name, position title, job title. Examples: "Athlete Role namedPosition 'Quarterback'", "Employee Role namedPosition 'Senior Software Engineer'", "Board Member Role namedPosition 'Treasurer'". Distinct from roleName, which is a more general description of a role.

candidates.label: owns
candidates.comment: A thing that is owned by an organization or person. Also called possesses, holds title to, has ownership of. Examples: "John Doe owns 'a car'", "Acme Corp owns 'a patent'", "Sarah owns 'her house'". Distinct from memberOf, which describes membership in a group.

candidates.label: member
candidates.comment: A member relation between an organization or program membership and an organization or person belonging to it. Also called: belongs to, is a part of, participant in. Examples: "Club Organization member John Doe", "Team ProgramMembership member Jane Smith", "Alliance Organization member Partner Company". Distinct from memberOf, which expresses the inverse relationship.

candidates.label: memberOf
candidates.comment: A membership relation between an organization or person and the organization or program membership they belong to. Also called: belongs to, is a member of, affiliated with. Examples: "John Doe memberOf 'Local Sports Club'", "Acme Corp memberOf 'Industry Association'", "Jane Smith memberOf 'Premium Membership Tier'". Distinct from member, which expresses the inverse relationship.

candidates.label: endorsee
candidates.comment: An endorsee relation between an endorse action and the person or organization being supported. Also called "supported entity", "beneficiary", "recipient of endorsement". Examples: "Endorse action endorsee 'Candidate A'", "Endorse action endorsee 'Charity B'", "Endorse action endorsee 'Product C'". Distinct from endorsers, which are the people or organizations providing the endorsement.

candidates.label: hasCredential
candidates.comment: A credential relation between an organization or person and an awarded credential. Also called holds credential, awarded credential, possesses credential. Examples: "A person has a credential as a licensed engineer.", "An organization has a credential for business excellence.", "The professional has a credential in data science."

candidates.label: members
candidates.comment: A member relation between an organization or program membership and an organization or person belonging to it. Also called: includes members, comprises, consists of. Examples: "Club Organization members John Doe", "Team ProgramMembership members Jane Smith", "Alliance Organization members Partner Company". Distinct from member, which is a singular form and essentially the same concept.

candidates.label: employee
candidates.comment: An employment relation between an organization and a person who works for it. Also called "works for", "staff member", "on staff". Examples: "Organization 'Google' employee 'Sundar Pichai'", "Company 'Acme Corp' employee 'Jane Doe'", "Restaurant 'The Bistro' employee 'Chef John'". Distinct from member, which indicates a general affiliation rather than an employment relationship.

candidates.label: hiringOrganization
candidates.comment: A hiring organization relation between a job posting and the organization or person offering the job. Also called employer, recruiting organization, job provider. Examples: "A job posting has a hiring organization 'Acme Corp'.", "The position is offered by a hiring organization.", "This job posting lists the hiring organization."

relations.definition: To be connected or associated with something, often in a significant or important way.
relations.embedding_query_text: involved: To be connected or associated with something, often in a significant or important way.

chosen_property.label: isInvolvedIn
chosen_property.definition: To be connected or associated with something, often in a significant or important way.
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property fits the relation of involvement between an event and a city

candidates.label: isRelatedTo
candidates.comment: A general association relation between two products or services that have some unspecified connection. Also called associated with, connected to, linked to, relevant to. Examples: A smartphone isRelatedTo 'a smart watch'. A car service isRelatedTo 'car insurance'. A book isRelatedTo 'a movie adaptation'. Distinct from isSimilarTo, which implies functional similarity, and isAccessoryOrSparePartFor or isConsumableFor, which imply specific functional dependencies. This is a very general relation.

candidates.label: affiliation
candidates.comment: An affiliation relation between a person and an organization they are associated with. Also called associated with, member of, works for, belongs to. Examples: "A professor's affiliation is 'Harvard University'.", "A player's affiliation is 'Local Soccer Club'." Distinct from alumniOf, which specifies a past association with an educational organization.

candidates.label: events
candidates.comment: An events association relation between an organization or place and the events connected to it. Also called "associated events", "related events", "features events". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' events 'Art Exhibition, Lecture Series'", "Place 'Park' events 'Summer Festival, Winter Fair'", "Company 'Tech Solutions' events 'Annual Conference, Product Launch'". Distinct from event, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: event
candidates.comment: An event association relation between an action, organization, or place and an event connected to it. Also called "associated event", "related event", "features event". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' event 'Art Exhibition'", "Place 'Park' event 'Summer Festival'", "Inform action event 'Meeting Reminder'". Distinct from events, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: connectedTo
candidates.comment: A connection relation between an anatomical structure and other anatomical structures it is connected to. Also called "linked to", "adjoins", "connects with". Examples: "Femur anatomical structure connectedTo Tibia", "Brain anatomical structure connectedTo Spinal cord".

candidates.label: associatedDisease
candidates.comment: A medical condition or URL representing a disease linked to a biochemical entity. Also called: related disease, disease connection, disease association. Examples: "BioChemEntity 'Insulin' associatedDisease 'Diabetes'", "BioChemEntity 'Gene X' associatedDisease 'Cancer'", "BioChemEntity 'Drug Y' associatedDisease 'Hypertension'."

candidates.label: significantLink
candidates.comment: A prominent and frequently clicked non-navigation URL found on a webpage. Also called important link, key URL, primary link. Examples: `Product Page` significantLink `URL to "Add to Cart"`, `Article Page` significantLink `URL to "Download PDF"`, `Homepage` significantLink `URL to "About Us"`. Distinct from `significantLinks`, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: lifeEvent
candidates.comment: A life event relation between a person and a significant event in their life. Also called: significant event, personal milestone, biographical event. Examples: "John Doe lifeEvent Baptism", "Jane Smith lifeEvent Graduation Ceremony", "Family lifeEvent Wedding".

candidates.label: participant
candidates.comment: A collaborative relation between an action and an organization or person who indirectly participated in it. Also called collaborated with, involved, assisted by, co-agent. Examples: A writing action has a participant co-author. A research project has a participant researcher. A meeting has a participant attendee. Distinct from agent, which is the primary actor of an action.

candidates.label: relatedTo
candidates.comment: A familial relation between two people, representing a generic family connection. Also called family member, kin, relative. Examples: "John is related to 'Jane'.", "Mary is related to 'Tom'.", "Aunt Sally is related to 'Nephew Bob'."

relations.definition: To be the reason or explanation for something happening or existing.
relations.embedding_query_text: caused by: To be the reason or explanation for something happening or existing.

candidates.label: source
candidates.comment: A causal relation between an instantaneous event and the thing that initiated or caused it. Also called "originates from", "caused by", "event trigger", "event origin". Examples: "The explosion's source was a gas leak", "The alarm's source was a smoke detector", "The data breach's source was a phishing attack."

candidates.label: cause
candidates.comment: A causal relation between a medical condition and its medical cause. Also called "etiology", "origin", "caused by". Examples: "Flu medical condition cause Influenza virus", "Heart attack medical condition cause Coronary artery disease". Distinct from causeOf, which describes what a medical cause leads to, whereas cause describes what leads to a condition.

candidates.label: causeOf
candidates.comment: A causal relation between a medical cause and the medical entity (condition, complication, symptom) it produces. Also called "results in", "leads to", "produces". Examples: "Influenza virus medical causeOf Flu", "Smoking medical causeOf Lung cancer". Distinct from cause, which describes what leads to a condition, whereas causeOf describes what a medical cause leads to.

candidates.label: possibleComplication
candidates.comment: A medical attribute describing a potential unexpected and unfavorable evolution or outcome of a medical condition. Also called potential adverse event, risk, secondary condition, complication risk. Examples: Diabetes has a possible complication of 'kidney failure'. Surgery has a possible complication of 'infection'. A medical condition has a possible complication of 'worsening symptoms'.

candidates.label: error
candidates.comment: An error relation between a failed action and the thing providing more information on the cause of the failure. Also called "failure cause", "problem details", "issue description". Examples: "Action 'Payment' error 'Insufficient Funds'", "Action 'Login' error 'Invalid Credentials'", "Action 'File Upload' error 'File Too Large'". Distinct from errorCode, which is a specific code for the error.

candidates.label: about
candidates.comment: A subject matter relation between an entity (e.g., a creative work, event, or communication) and the topic it concerns. Also called concerning, regarding, on the topic of, related to. Examples: "A book about quantum physics.", "A lecture about climate change.", "A certification about data privacy."

candidates.label: ratingExplanation
candidates.comment: A rating explanation relation between a rating and a brief text providing context or justification for the rating. Also called rating justification, explanation for rating, rating context. Examples: "A product rating includes a rating explanation 'The battery life was excellent, but the camera was disappointing'.", "A fact-check rating has a rating explanation 'The claim was partially true, lacking full context'.", "A service rating has a rating explanation 'The staff were friendly, but wait times were long'."

candidates.label: subjectOf
candidates.comment: A thematic relation between a thing and a creative work or event that is about it. Also called "topic of", "depicted in", "featured in", "covered by". Examples: "The person is subjectOf a biography", "The historical event is subjectOf a documentary", "This concept is subjectOf a research paper."

candidates.label: answerExplanation
candidates.comment: An answer explanation relation between an answer and a comment or web content providing a detailed clarification or step-by-step reasoning. Also called solution explanation, answer justification, detailed response. Examples: "An answer's answer explanation details the calculation steps.", "The correct answer's explanation clarifies the underlying principle."

candidates.label: result
candidates.comment: The outcome or product generated by an action. Also called outcome, product, output, consequence. Examples: `WriteAction` result `Book`, `CookAction` result `Meal`, `CreateAction` result `Artwork`. Distinct from `resultComment` and `resultReview` which are specific types of results.

relations.definition: To express an opinion or make a statement about something.
relations.embedding_query_text: commented on: To express an opinion or make a statement about something.

instances: Ursula von der Leyen -> Migrant crossing

chosen_property.label: comment
chosen_property.justification: Matches the relation of making a comment about something

candidates.label: parentItem
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a discussion item and its preceding item or a creative work it comments on. Also called part of, replies to, refers to, is a response to. Examples: A comment is a parent item of another comment. A question is a parent item of an answer. An answer is a parent item of a follow-up comment. Distinct from comment, which points from something to a comment about it.

candidates.label: discusses
candidates.comment: A discussion relation between a user comment and the creative work it is associated with. Also called "comments on", "pertains to", "about". Examples: "User comment 'Great movie!' discusses 'The Matrix'", "Blog post comment discusses 'Article on AI'", "Review discusses 'New Album by Artist X'". Distinct from discussionUrl, which is a link to the page containing comments about a creative work.

candidates.label: resultComment
candidates.comment: The specific comment created or sent as the outcome of a comment or reply action. Also called generated comment, comment outcome, produced comment. Examples: `CommentAction on Article` resultComment `User's Comment Text`, `ReplyAction to Forum Post` resultComment `Reply Comment`, `ReviewAction` resultComment `Reviewer's Feedback`. Distinct from `result`, which is a general outcome of any action.

candidates.label: comment
candidates.comment: A feedback relation between a creative work or RSVP action and a user-generated comment. Also called "user comment", "feedback", "review". Examples: "Article comment 'Great read!'", "Event RSVP comment 'Looking forward to it!'". Distinct from commentText, which is the text content of the comment itself.

candidates.label: answerExplanation
candidates.comment: An answer explanation relation between an answer and a comment or web content providing a detailed clarification or step-by-step reasoning. Also called solution explanation, answer justification, detailed response. Examples: "An answer's answer explanation details the calculation steps.", "The correct answer's explanation clarifies the underlying principle."

candidates.label: commentCount
candidates.comment: A quantitative measurement for a creative work, indicating the total number of comments it has received. Also called "number of comments", "comment total", "feedback count". Examples: "Blog post commentCount 15", "Article commentCount 200".

candidates.label: commentText
candidates.comment: A textual content relation for user comments, providing the actual text of the comment. Also called "comment content", "message text", "user feedback text". Examples: "User comment commentText 'This is a very insightful article.'", "Review commentText 'Product arrived quickly and works great.'". Distinct from comment, which refers to the comment object itself, whereas commentText is its textual content.

candidates.label: commentTime
candidates.comment: A temporal specification for user comments, indicating the date or date and time when the comment was made. Also called "comment date", "posted time", "submission time". Examples: "User comment commentTime '2023-10-26T10:30:00'", "Review commentTime '2023-09-15'".

candidates.label: downvoteCount
candidates.comment: A downvote count relation between a comment and the integer representing the number of downvotes it has received. Also called "dislike count", "negative votes". Examples: "Comment 'This is wrong' downvoteCount '5'", "Answer downvoteCount '2'", "Review downvoteCount '10'".

candidates.label: upvoteCount
candidates.comment: An upvote count relation between a comment and the number of upvotes it has received. Also called positive votes, likes count, approval count. Examples: "Comment upvoteCount '15'", "Answer upvoteCount '100'", "Question upvoteCount '5'".

relations.definition: To be in charge of or to direct an organization, group, or activity.
relations.embedding_query_text: leads: To be in charge of or to direct an organization, group, or activity.

chosen_property.label: leads
chosen_property.definition: To be in charge of or to direct an organization, group, or activity.
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property fits the relation of leading a police station

candidates.label: agent
candidates.comment: An agent relation between an action and the organization or person who directly performs or drives it. Also called performer, doer, initiator, actor. Examples: "A 'write book' action's agent is 'John Doe'.", "A 'deliver package' action's agent is 'Delivery Service Inc'."

candidates.label: participant
candidates.comment: A collaborative relation between an action and an organization or person who indirectly participated in it. Also called collaborated with, involved, assisted by, co-agent. Examples: A writing action has a participant co-author. A research project has a participant researcher. A meeting has a participant attendee. Distinct from agent, which is the primary actor of an action.

candidates.label: organizer
candidates.comment: An organization or person responsible for organizing an event. Also called event planner, host, coordinator, promoter. Examples: "Conference X organizer 'Acme Events Inc.'", "Concert Y organizer 'Live Nation'", "Workshop Z organizer 'Jane Doe'". Distinct from performer, who participates in the event.

candidates.label: sender
candidates.comment: The audience, organization, or person initiating and transmitting a message or action. Also called originator, dispatcher, message source, sender of message. Examples: `Email Message` sender `John Doe`, `ReceiveAction` sender `Customer Service`, `Broadcast Message` sender `News Organization`. Distinct from `recipient`, which is the receiving party.

candidates.label: followee
candidates.comment: A followee relation between a follow action and the person or organization that is being followed. Also called: followed entity, subject of follow, target of follow. Examples: "User A follows User B" followee "User B", "Fan follows Band X" followee "Band X", "Journalist follows News Organization Y" followee "News Organization Y". Distinct from follows, which is the general social relation.

candidates.label: sourceOrganization
candidates.comment: An affiliation relation between a creative work and the organization on whose behalf its creator was working. Also called "commissioning organization", "producing organization", "organization behind", "publisher organization". Examples: "The research paper's sourceOrganization was MIT", "The documentary's sourceOrganization was BBC", "This report's sourceOrganization is the World Health Organization."

candidates.label: member
candidates.comment: A member relation between an organization or program membership and an organization or person belonging to it. Also called: belongs to, is a part of, participant in. Examples: "Club Organization member John Doe", "Team ProgramMembership member Jane Smith", "Alliance Organization member Partner Company". Distinct from memberOf, which expresses the inverse relationship.

candidates.label: producer
candidates.comment: A creative role relation between a creative work and the person or organization responsible for its production. Also called production company, executive producer, creator, maker. Examples: A movie has a producer 'Steven Spielberg'. A music album has a producer 'Universal Music Group'. A TV series has a producer 'Shonda Rhimes'. Distinct from director, who is responsible for the creative vision.

candidates.label: roleName
candidates.comment: The specific designation or title of a role performed by a person or organization. Also called role title, position name, function name. Examples: `Person in Movie` roleName `"Actor"`, `Team Member` roleName `"Quarterback"`, `Project Contributor` roleName `"Lead Developer"`.

candidates.label: director
candidates.comment: A creative leadership relation between a clip, creative work season, episode, event, movie, or video game and a person who directed it. Also called: directed by, filmmaker, showrunner. Examples: "Movie" director "Steven Spielberg", "TV Episode" director "Ava DuVernay", "Video Game" director "Hideo Kojima". Distinct from directors, which is a plural property for multiple directors.

chosen_property.label: supports
chosen_property.definition: To give help or assistance to someone or something.
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property fits the relation of supporting a country

candidates.label: inSupportOf
candidates.comment: A support relation between a thesis and the qualification, candidature, degree, or application it supports. Also called supports for, for the purpose of, in aid of. Examples: "A thesis is in support of a PhD degree.", "The research is in support of a qualification.", "This thesis is written in support of an application."

candidates.label: productSupported
candidates.comment: A support relation between a contact point and the product or service it provides support for. Also called supports product, provides support for, related to product. Examples: "Apple Support contact point supports iPhone.", "Microsoft customer service supports Windows.", "Help desk supports enterprise software."

candidates.label: supportingData
candidates.comment: A data relation between a software application and the data feed that provides supplementary information or content. Also called "supplementary data", "data feed for", "application data source". Examples: "The mapping application has supportingData a traffic data feed", "The software application's supportingData is a weather feed", "This program uses supportingData for real-time updates."

candidates.label: endorsers
candidates.comment: An endorsers relation between a diet and the people or organizations that support or recommend it. Also called "supporters", "advocates", "recommenders". Examples: "Diet 'Mediterranean Diet' endorsers 'World Health Organization'", "Diet 'Vegan Diet' endorsers 'PETA'", "Diet 'Keto Diet' endorsers 'Dr. X'". Distinct from endorsee, which is the entity being supported.

candidates.label: sponsor
candidates.comment: A support relation between an entity (creative work, event, grant, study, organization, or person) and the person or organization providing financial or other backing. Also called "funded by", "supported by", "patron", "underwritten by". Examples: "The event has sponsor Acme Corp", "The medical study's sponsor is the NIH", "This artist has sponsor a private foundation."

candidates.label: availableLanguage
candidates.comment: A language that can be used with or at an item, service, or place. Also called: supported language, language option, communication language. Examples: "ContactPoint 'Support' availableLanguage 'en'", "Course 'Programming' availableLanguage 'es'", "LodgingBusiness 'Hotel' availableLanguage 'fr'". Distinct from inLanguage, which specifies the language of the content itself.

candidates.label: accessibilityAPI
candidates.comment: An accessibility API compatibility relation between a creative work and the accessibility API it supports. Also called API support, accessibility interface. Examples: "A software application's accessibility API is 'AT-SPI'.", "A web page's accessibility API is 'ARIA'."

candidates.label: operatingSystem
candidates.comment: An operating system supported by a software application. Also called supported OS, compatible operating system, runs on. Examples: "Software X operatingSystem 'Windows 10'", "App Y operatingSystem 'iOS 16'", "Game Z operatingSystem 'macOS Ventura'".

candidates.label: countriesSupported
candidates.comment: A geographical availability relation between a software application and the countries where it is supported. Also called: supported regions, available in, operational in. Examples: "App X" countries supported "USA, Canada", "Software Y" countries supported "Germany, France, UK", "Game Z" countries supported "Japan, South Korea". Distinct from countriesNotSupported, which lists where the application is not supported.

candidates.label: contributor
candidates.comment: A secondary participation relation for a creative work or event, indicating an organization or person who contributed to it. Also called "additional contributor", "supporting role", "collaborator". Examples: "Book creative work contributor 'Editor Jane Doe'", "Conference event contributor 'Sponsor Acme Corp'". Distinct from author or creator, which typically denote primary responsibility.

chosen_property.label: isInContactWith
chosen_property.definition: To be in communication or connection with someone or something.
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property fits the relation of being in contact with a country

candidates.label: contactPoint
candidates.comment: A communication relation between a health insurance plan, organization, or person and one of their contact points. Also called "contact info", "point of contact", "reach at". Examples: "Company organization contactPoint 'Customer Service'", "Person contactPoint 'Email Address'". Distinct from contactPoints, which is the plural form, though semantically similar.

candidates.label: contactPoints
candidates.comment: A communication relation between an organization or person and their various contact points. Also called "contact information", "points of contact", "ways to reach". Examples: "Company organization contactPoints [Customer Service, Press Office]", "Person contactPoints [Email, Phone]". Distinct from contactPoint, which is the singular form, though semantically similar.

candidates.label: email
candidates.comment: An email address relation between a contact point, organization, or person and their electronic mail address. Also called "contact email", "email contact", "electronic mail". Examples: "Organization 'Acme Corp' email 'info@acmecorp.com'", "Person 'John Doe' email 'john.doe@example.com'", "Customer service contactPoint email 'support@example.com'".

candidates.label: applicationContact
candidates.comment: An application contact relation between a job posting and the contact point for additional information. Also called job contact, hiring contact, recruitment contact. Examples: "A job posting's application contact is the 'HR Department email'.", "The job's application contact is a 'recruiter's phone number'."

candidates.label: contactOption
candidates.comment: A feature relation for a contact point, indicating an available option such as a toll-free number or accessibility support. Also called "contact feature", "available option", "support option". Examples: "Customer service contact point contactOption 'TollFree'", "Accessibility contact point contactOption 'HearingImpairedSupported'".

candidates.label: contactType
candidates.comment: A classification relation for a contact point, specifying its purpose or kind. Also called "type of contact", "contact purpose", "department". Examples: "Phone number contact point contactType 'Sales'", "Email address contact point contactType 'Support'".

candidates.label: homeLocation
candidates.comment: A home location relation between a person and their residential contact point or place. Also called residence, dwelling, home address. Examples: "A person has a home location in London.", "Her home location is a specific address.", "The individual's home location is a contact point."

candidates.label: productSupported
candidates.comment: A support relation between a contact point and the product or service it provides support for. Also called supports product, provides support for, related to product. Examples: "Apple Support contact point supports iPhone.", "Microsoft customer service supports Windows.", "Help desk supports enterprise software."

candidates.label: connectedTo
candidates.comment: A connection relation between an anatomical structure and other anatomical structures it is connected to. Also called "linked to", "adjoins", "connects with". Examples: "Femur anatomical structure connectedTo Tibia", "Brain anatomical structure connectedTo Spinal cord".

candidates.label: recipient
candidates.comment: A recipient relation between an action (like sending or paying) and the audience, contact point, organization, or person receiving it. Also called receiver, intended for, sent to. Examples: "A message has a recipient 'John Doe'.", "A donation has a recipient 'Charity Organization'.", "A payment has a recipient 'Vendor Inc.'."

chosen_property.label: tightensBorderWith
chosen_property.definition: To strengthen or reinforce the border between two entities.
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property fits the relation of tightening a border

candidates.label: geoTouches
candidates.comment: A geo touches relation representing a symmetric spatial relationship where two geometries or places share at least one boundary point but no interior points. Also called: borders, adjoins, meets at boundary. Examples: "Country A" geo touches "Country B", "Property Line 1" geo touches "Property Line 2", "Lake Shore" geo touches "Land Mass". Distinct from geoIntersects, which can share interior points.

candidates.label: geoIntersects
candidates.comment: A geo intersects relation representing a spatial relationship where two geometries or places share at least one common point. Also called: overlaps with, touches, crosses. Examples: "River 'Thames'" geo intersects "City 'London'", "Road 'Main Street'" geo intersects "Park 'Central Park'", "Country 'USA'" geo intersects "Country 'Canada'". Distinct from geoDisjoint, which has no points in common.

candidates.label: insertion
candidates.comment: An anatomical attachment relation between a muscle and the anatomical structure where it inserts, or the structure it moves. Also called attachment point, insertion point, moves, connects to. Examples: The biceps muscle has an insertion on the 'radius bone'. The deltoid muscle has an insertion on the 'humerus'. The gastrocnemius muscle has an insertion on the 'calcaneus'. Distinct from origin, which is the fixed attachment point of a muscle.

candidates.label: line
candidates.comment: A line representation relation between a geographic shape and its textual description as a series of points. Also called: path coordinates, point series, geographic line. Examples: "Road Segment line '34.05,-118.25 34.06,-118.26'", "River Path line '40.71,-74.00 40.72,-74.01'", "Borderline line '50.00,0.00 51.00,1.00'".

candidates.label: connectedTo
candidates.comment: A connection relation between an anatomical structure and other anatomical structures it is connected to. Also called "linked to", "adjoins", "connects with". Examples: "Femur anatomical structure connectedTo Tibia", "Brain anatomical structure connectedTo Spinal cord".

candidates.label: geoOverlaps
candidates.comment: A geo overlaps relation representing a spatial relationship where two geometries or places share some, but not all, common points. Also called: partially overlaps, shares area with, intersects partially. Examples: "City Park" geo overlaps "Residential Area", "Forest Reserve" geo overlaps "Hiking Trail Network", "Economic Zone A" geo overlaps "Economic Zone B". Distinct from geoContains (one fully encloses the other) and geoDisjoint (no common points).

candidates.label: legislationTransposes
candidates.comment: A transposition relation between two pieces of legislation, where one fulfills the objectives of the other through implementation measures. Also called: transposes, implements directive, fulfills objectives of. Examples: "Member State Law legislationTransposes EU Directive", "Regional Act legislationTransposes National Regulation", "Local Ordinance legislationTransposes State Mandate". Distinct from legislationEnsuresImplementationOf, which implies modifying national legislations to avoid contradiction, rather than fulfilling objectives.

candidates.label: legislationEnsuresImplementationOf
candidates.comment: An implementation assurance relation between two pieces of legislation, where one ensures the implementation of the other by modifying national laws. Also called: implements, ensures compliance with, enforces. Examples: "National Law A legislationEnsuresImplementationOf EU Regulation B", "State Statute legislationEnsuresImplementationOf Federal Act", "Local Ordinance legislationEnsuresImplementationOf Regional Directive". Distinct from legislationTransposes, which specifically refers to fulfilling objectives by passing implementation measures.

candidates.label: containsPlace
candidates.comment: A spatial containment relation between a place and another smaller place that it contains. Also called "includes place", "encompasses", "holds". Examples: "Country 'France' containsPlace 'Paris'", "City 'Paris' containsPlace 'Eiffel Tower'". Distinct from containedIn or containedInPlace, which are the inverse relations.

candidates.label: travelBans
candidates.comment: A travel bans relation between a special announcement and information regarding restrictions on travel. Also called travel restrictions, ban on travel, travel advisories. Examples: "SpecialAnnouncement travelBans 'https://example.com/travel-restrictions'", "SpecialAnnouncement travelBans 'All international travel is suspended.'", "SpecialAnnouncement travelBans 'https://who.int/travel-guidance'".

relations.relation_phrase: threatens to suspend Schengen agreement with
relations.embedding_query_text: threatens to suspend Schengen agreement with:

chosen_property.label: threatensToSuspendSchengenAgreementWith
chosen_property.definition: To threaten to stop or cancel the Schengen agreement with another entity.
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property fits the relation of threatening to suspend an agreement

candidates.label: travelBans
candidates.comment: A travel bans relation between a special announcement and information regarding restrictions on travel. Also called travel restrictions, ban on travel, travel advisories. Examples: "SpecialAnnouncement travelBans 'https://example.com/travel-restrictions'", "SpecialAnnouncement travelBans 'All international travel is suspended.'", "SpecialAnnouncement travelBans 'https://who.int/travel-guidance'".

candidates.label: safetyConsideration
candidates.comment: Any potential safety concerns, interactions, or adverse reactions associated with a dietary supplement. Also called supplement warnings, safety warnings, adverse effects. Examples: `St. John's Wort` safetyConsideration `"May interact with antidepressants"`, `Creatine Supplement` safetyConsideration `"Not recommended for individuals with kidney issues"`, `Vitamin D Supplement` safetyConsideration `"Avoid excessive dosage"`.

candidates.label: reservationStatus
candidates.comment: A reservation status relation between a reservation and its current state, such as confirmed or cancelled. Also called booking status, status of reservation. Examples: "A flight reservation has a reservation status 'Confirmed'.", "A hotel booking has a reservation status 'Pending'.", "A restaurant reservation has a reservation status 'Cancelled'."

candidates.label: validUntil
candidates.comment: A valid until relation between a permit and the date it ceases to be valid. Also called permit expiration date, permit end date, validity end date. Examples: "Permit validUntil '2024-06-30'", "Permit validUntil '2025-01-01'", "Permit validUntil '2023-12-31'". Distinct from validThrough, which is a more general property for various items.

candidates.label: legislationEnsuresImplementationOf
candidates.comment: An implementation assurance relation between two pieces of legislation, where one ensures the implementation of the other by modifying national laws. Also called: implements, ensures compliance with, enforces. Examples: "National Law A legislationEnsuresImplementationOf EU Regulation B", "State Statute legislationEnsuresImplementationOf Federal Act", "Local Ordinance legislationEnsuresImplementationOf Regional Directive". Distinct from legislationTransposes, which specifically refers to fulfilling objectives by passing implementation measures.

candidates.label: expectedArrivalUntil
candidates.comment: An expected arrival until relation between a parcel delivery and the latest date or datetime the package is anticipated to arrive. Also called: latest arrival, maximum delivery date, estimated end arrival. Examples: "Amazon Order #123" expected arrival until "2023-10-28", "UPS Package #456" expected arrival until "2023-10-27T17:00:00", "International Shipment" expected arrival until "2023-11-05". Distinct from expectedArrivalFrom, which is the earliest arrival date.

candidates.label: meetsEmissionStandard
candidates.comment: An emission standard compliance relation between a vehicle and the qualitative value, text, or URL indicating the emission standard it meets. Also called: emission compliant, environmentally certified, low emission. Examples: "Electric Car meetsEmissionStandard 'Zero Emission'", "New Diesel Car meetsEmissionStandard 'Euro 6'", "Hybrid Vehicle meetsEmissionStandard 'CARB LEV III'".

candidates.label: securityClearanceRequirement
candidates.comment: A description or URL detailing the security clearance level or requirements necessary for a job. Also called clearance needed, security level, job clearance. Examples: `Government Job` securityClearanceRequirement `"Top Secret"`, `Defense Contractor Role` securityClearanceRequirement `URL to clearance guidelines`, `IT Security Position` securityClearanceRequirement `"Secret Clearance Required"`.

candidates.label: warning
candidates.comment: A warning relation between a drug and any FDA or other safety advisories. Also called drug warning, safety advisory, health alert. Examples: "Drug warning 'May cause drowsiness.'", "Drug warning 'https://fda.gov/drug-warnings/xyz'", "Medication warning 'Do not exceed recommended dose.'".

candidates.label: subReservation
candidates.comment: A component relation between a reservation package and the individual reservations it comprises. Also called "included reservation", "package component reservation", "individual booking". Examples: "The travel package has subReservation a flight booking", "The hotel package's subReservation is a spa appointment", "This reservation package includes multiple subReservation items."

chosen_property.label: requests
chosen_property.definition: To ask or demand something from someone or something.
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property fits the relation of requesting something from a country

candidates.label: seeks
candidates.comment: A demand for specific products or services expressed by an organization or person. Also called desires, looks for, requests, requires. Examples: `Company X` seeks `Demand for Software Developers`, `Person Y` seeks `Demand for Used Car`, `Organization Z` seeks `Demand for Consulting Services`. Distinct from `offers`, which is about what is provided.

candidates.label: httpMethod
candidates.comment: An HTTP method relation between an entry point and the appropriate HTTP method for a request. Also called HTTP verb, request method, API method. Examples: "An entry point has an HTTP method 'GET'.", "The API endpoint uses an HTTP method 'POST'.", "This entry point specifies the HTTP method."

candidates.label: rsvpResponse
candidates.comment: The specific response (e.g., Yes, No, Maybe) provided to an RSVP request. Also called RSVP status, attendance response, invitation reply. Examples: `Wedding RSVP` rsvpResponse `RsvpResponseType: Yes`, `Conference RSVP` rsvpResponse `RsvpResponseType: No`, `Party Invitation` rsvpResponse `RsvpResponseType: Maybe`.

candidates.label: itemOffered
candidates.comment: A transaction subject relation between a demand or offer and the specific item, product, service, or event being requested or provided. Also called offered item, demanded item, subject of offer, product/service offered. Examples: An offer has an itemOffered of 'a new car'. A demand has an itemOffered of 'web design service'. An offer has an itemOffered of 'a concert ticket'. Distinct from itemReviewed, which is the subject of a review, not an offer/demand.

candidates.label: offers
candidates.comment: An offer or demand related to a product, service, event, or other item. Also called available offers, related offers, product offers. Examples: "Product X offers 'Offer to sell'", "Service Y offers 'Demand for service'", "Event Z offers 'Offer for tickets'". Distinct from hasOfferCatalog, which points to a catalog of offers.

candidates.label: permissions
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute detailing the permissions required for a software application to function. Also called access requirements, app permissions, authorization needs. Examples: A mobile app requires permissions for 'full internet access'. A software application requires permissions for 'access to camera'. A game requires permissions for 'storage access'.

candidates.label: applicantLocationRequirements
candidates.comment: An applicant location requirements relation between a job posting and the administrative area(s) from which candidates can apply, especially for remote positions. Also called remote work location, eligible application region, telecommuting area. Examples: "A job posting's applicant location requirements include 'Anywhere in the US'.", "The remote job's applicant location requirements are 'Europe'."

candidates.label: expectsAcceptanceOf
candidates.comment: An expects acceptance of relation between an action access specification, consume action, or media subscription and an offer that must be accepted before the action can be performed. Also called: requires offer, prerequisite offer, conditional offer. Examples: "Watch Movie Action" expects acceptance of "Movie Purchase Offer", "Download Software Action" expects acceptance of "Software License Offer", "Access Premium Content" expects acceptance of "Subscription Offer".

candidates.label: suggestedAnswer
candidates.comment: A proposed response or set of responses to a question. Also called "possible answer", "proposed solution", "answer option", "response to question". Examples: "The question has suggestedAnswer 'Yes'", "The quiz question's suggestedAnswer is a multiple-choice list", "This question provides a suggestedAnswer for users."

candidates.label: question
candidates.comment: A question relation between an ask action and the specific question being posed. Also called asked question, inquiry. Examples: "An ask action involves the question 'What is the capital of France?'.", "A survey asks the question 'How satisfied are you with our service?'.", "A forum post poses the question 'How do I fix this error?'."

chosen_property.label: containsPlace
chosen_property.justification: Matches the spatial containment relationship described

candidates.label: containsPlace
candidates.comment: A spatial containment relation between a place and another smaller place that it contains. Also called "includes place", "encompasses", "holds". Examples: "Country 'France' containsPlace 'Paris'", "City 'Paris' containsPlace 'Eiffel Tower'". Distinct from containedIn or containedInPlace, which are the inverse relations.

candidates.label: containedInPlace
candidates.comment: A spatial containment relation between a place and the larger place that contains it. Also called "located in", "part of", "within". Examples: "City 'Paris' containedInPlace 'France'", "Building 'Eiffel Tower' containedInPlace 'Paris'". Distinct from containedIn, which is a synonym, and containsPlace, which is the inverse.

candidates.label: geoWithin
candidates.comment: A geo within relation representing a spatial relationship where a geometry or place is located entirely inside the interior of another containing geometry or place. Also called: is inside, contained in, located within. Examples: "City 'Paris'" geo within "Country 'France'", "Office 'Suite 100'" geo within "Building 'Empire State'", "State 'California'" geo within "Country 'USA'". Distinct from geoContains, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: hasPOS
candidates.comment: A point-of-sale relation between an organization or person and a place where they operate a point of sale. Also called operates POS, sales location, retail point. Examples: "An organization has a POS in New York.", "The vendor has a POS at the market.", "This company operates multiple POS locations."

candidates.label: geoCoveredBy
candidates.comment: A geo covered by relation representing a spatial relationship where a geometry or place is entirely covered by another geometry or place. Also called: is covered by, lies within, is contained by. Examples: "City 'Paris'" geo covered by "Country 'France'", "Lake 'Superior'" geo covered by "North America", "House '123 Main St'" geo covered by "City 'Springfield'". Distinct from geoCovers, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: containedIn
candidates.comment: A spatial containment relation between a place and the larger place that contains it. Also called "located in", "part of", "within". Examples: "City 'Paris' containedIn 'France'", "Building 'Eiffel Tower' containedIn 'Paris'". Distinct from containedInPlace, which is a synonym, and containsPlace, which is the inverse.

candidates.label: addressLocality
candidates.comment: An address locality relation between a postal address and the city or town where it is situated. Also called city, town, municipality. Examples: "A postal address's address locality is 'Mountain View'.", "The address locality is 'London'."

candidates.label: hasDriveThroughService
candidates.comment: A drive-through service availability relation for a place, indicating whether it offers services accessible by driving through. Also called offers drive-through, drive-through available, drive-in service. Examples: "A restaurant has drive-through service.", "A testing facility has drive-through service.", "The bank has drive-through service for transactions."

candidates.label: serviceArea
candidates.comment: The geographical region or area where a service is available or provided. Also called service region, coverage area, operational zone. Examples: `Delivery Service` serviceArea `GeoShape: New York City`, `Local Business` serviceArea `AdministrativeArea: California`, `Customer Support` serviceArea `Place: United States`. Distinct from `areaServed`, which is a more general property for things like organizations.

candidates.label: hasParticipationOffer
candidates.comment: A participation offer relation between an event and an offer to participate in it. Also called call for participation, participation opportunity, event entry offer. Examples: "An event has a participation offer for speakers.", "The conference has a participation offer for proposals.", "This festival includes a participation offer for performers.". Distinct from hasSponsorshipOffer, which is an offer to sponsor the event.

chosen_property.label: blames
chosen_property.definition: To hold responsible or accuse someone or something for a fault or mistake.
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property fits the relation of blaming a statement

candidates.label: causeOf
candidates.comment: A causal relation between a medical cause and the medical entity (condition, complication, symptom) it produces. Also called "results in", "leads to", "produces". Examples: "Influenza virus medical causeOf Flu", "Smoking medical causeOf Lung cancer". Distinct from cause, which describes what leads to a condition, whereas causeOf describes what a medical cause leads to.

candidates.label: cause
candidates.comment: A causal relation between a medical condition and its medical cause. Also called "etiology", "origin", "caused by". Examples: "Flu medical condition cause Influenza virus", "Heart attack medical condition cause Coronary artery disease". Distinct from causeOf, which describes what a medical cause leads to, whereas cause describes what leads to a condition.

candidates.label: error
candidates.comment: An error relation between a failed action and the thing providing more information on the cause of the failure. Also called "failure cause", "problem details", "issue description". Examples: "Action 'Payment' error 'Insufficient Funds'", "Action 'Login' error 'Invalid Credentials'", "Action 'File Upload' error 'File Too Large'". Distinct from errorCode, which is a specific code for the error.

candidates.label: source
candidates.comment: A causal relation between an instantaneous event and the thing that initiated or caused it. Also called "originates from", "caused by", "event trigger", "event origin". Examples: "The explosion's source was a gas leak", "The alarm's source was a smoke detector", "The data breach's source was a phishing attack."

candidates.label: adverseOutcome
candidates.comment: An adverse outcome relation between a medical device or therapeutic procedure and a possible complication or side effect. Also called side effect, complication, negative reaction. Examples: "A surgery's adverse outcome is 'infection'.", "A medical device's adverse outcome is 'skin irritation'." Distinct from seriousAdverseOutcome, which is specifically for life-threatening or severe complications.

candidates.label: accountablePerson
candidates.comment: An accountable person relation between a creative work and the individual legally responsible for it. Also called legally responsible person, liable party, responsible individual. Examples: "A news article's accountable person is its editor-in-chief.", "A company report's accountable person is the CEO."

candidates.label: legislationResponsible
candidates.comment: A responsibility relation between a piece of legislation and the individual or organization accountable for its elaboration or inquiries. Also called: responsible for, overseen by, managed by. Examples: "Health Act legislationResponsible Ministry of Health", "Environmental Law legislationResponsible EPA", "Tax Reform legislationResponsible Treasury Department". Distinct from legislationPassedBy, which refers to the original enacting authority.

candidates.label: loser
candidates.comment: A losing participant relation between a win action and the person who lost. Also called: defeated participant, vanquished, runner-up. Examples: "Chess Match WinAction loser Opponent B", "Race WinAction loser Second Place Runner", "Debate WinAction loser Team B".

candidates.label: worstRating
candidates.comment: A worst rating relation between a rating and a number or text, specifying the lowest possible value within that rating system. Also called minimum rating, lowest score, bottom value. Examples: RatingSystem worstRating 1, ReviewRating worstRating "Terrible", StarRating worstRating 0. Distinct from bestRating, which specifies the highest possible value.

candidates.label: customerRemorseReturnShippingFeesAmount
candidates.comment: A return policy relation between a merchant return policy and the amount of shipping costs for a product returned due to customer remorse. Also called: remorse return shipping cost, customer-initiated return shipping fee, shipping fee for remorse return. Examples: "Online Purchase" customer remorse return shipping fees amount "10 USD", "Clothing Order" customer remorse return shipping fees amount "5 EUR", "Electronics Return" customer remorse return shipping fees amount "15 GBP". Distinct from customerRemorseReturnFees, which specifies the type of fees.
